nodes.title: Add optional hackathon banking adapter for ordinary completion ingress

nodes.body:
Supervisor review of the linked banking runtime at4be94bec. The native recorded-evidence verifier passed; deployed153a0391 and source-CI0afeaf0b production src trees are identical. The current full-test check is green. Those results do not cover the three route/build findings below.

The P1 revocation finding was reproduced against this exact head's actual configuredAdapter, workspace wrapper, worker-mode checks and route in an isolated TypeScript routing harness, with filesystem/auth/controller effects stubbed: a ready worker pinned to banking-workspace returns404 before the revoke handler runs. No paid workload or live service was changed.

The history/event finding is scoped to ordinary trusted-local/operator transport, whose individual banking histories are already intentionally protected by this adapter; banking customer credentials are denied the affected global endpoints. The default-packaging finding fails closed without policy and is an optional-integration claim/architecture defect, not an unauthenticated exploit. Please resolve the routing/projection holes and reconcile the default-build boundary before treating this integration as ready. This COMMENT is not independent approval because the authenticated account also authored the PR.

Follow-up at 805be7e0086714a551db804bbf9c82714dc3a746: the incremental change addresses all three findings from the previous review, with no new issue found in the focused diff.

P1 revoke: the exported route now dispatches through the generic extension. The optional banking adapter authenticates the original routing-free JWT request before binding the signed-policy workspace to a server-minted request, so the real workspace and worker gates can reach revocation for a nondefault banking workspace. The new exported POST test exercises the real JWT/store/admission/workspace/worker stack with external effects mocked, including revocation, abort, propagation and fail-closed negatives.

P2 projections: global conversation-chain and event routes now deny ordinary operator/local access to protected banking history before projection data access, as well as already-denied customer credentials. Tests cover query, slash and encoding variants. P2 packaging: the static banking controller import is removed from the default route in favor of generic dispatch; docs now accurately describe the inactive placeholder, and default Linux/Windows production builds pass.

Independent isolated exact-head archive testing passed three available suites (seven tests). Five more targeted suites could not load from the borrowed shared node_modules because it lacks this PR's dependencies; that is an environment limitation, not a test failure. Current exact-head CI has production builds, typecheck, lint, release safety, isolated tests and Windows artifact checks successful. The full main test job is still in progress, so its acceptance remains pending. The previous native 500-customer evidence was not replayed and does not prove the future six-call v0 graph.

This COMMENT is a technical follow-up; the author identity here cannot provide independent GitHub approval.

Final CI follow-up at 805be7e0086714a551db804bbf9c82714dc3a746: the full `test` job completed successfully. Its exact-head log shows PASS for `bankingRouteWiring.test.ts` (exported revoke route and nondefault workspace), `configuredAdapterBundles.test.ts` (protected projections), and `defaultRouteBoundary.test.ts` (generic optional route). Totals: 831 suites passed / 5 skipped; 7,594 tests passed / 11 skipped. All other required build/typecheck/lint/release/isolated/artifact checks succeeded; the separate diagnostic Persona memory profile was intentionally skipped.

Together with the source diff and earlier isolated checks, the P1 revoke-workspace finding and both P2 projection/optional-route findings are resolved at this head. This confirms the present runtime change and its covered tests; it does not prove Gloria's future six-call v0 intake/handoff workflow, bilingual product outcomes, or production banking actions. No native paid workload was replayed. This COMMENT is technical review, not independent GitHub approval.

nodes.title: Add protected sandbox banking action route

nodes.body:
Reviewed exact draft head `93d18466` as the companion to banking PR #16. The protected host-only route keeps model tools read-only, requires fresh ingress and an owned conversation, uses exact one-call grants, and reads persisted receipts/handoffs before success claims. It is a focused addition to the single-charge v0.

**CI gate:** GitHub's `typecheck` job fails after TypeScript passes because `node scripts/generate-api-inventory.mjs --check` finds the new `/v1/banking/action` route missing from the committed generated API inventory. Regenerate/commit the inventory and rerun the exact-head checks. The main test job was still running at review time.

**Product acceptance:** This route's tests mock MCP, while banking PR #16's frontend tests mock FLUJO. Keep the action control off until the companion P1 ledger/concurrency/revocation/handoff findings are fixed and one pinned browser→FLUJO→MCP ES/PT normal and human-required journey demonstrates a persisted case receipt or verified operator-pickup handoff. Do not count a locally stored HOF row as a human response or bank dispute.

Exact-head follow-up at `41ff3ca8905376759573bdcbe81862f98d74ca70`: the generated route inventory now includes `POST /v1/banking/action`, resolving my earlier typecheck/inventory finding. I checked the narrow route delta and ran the three focused banking suites locally (95 tests passed). Current CI has typecheck, lint, isolated tests, both production builds, and both release-safety jobs green; the broad `test` job is still running. I found no new FLUJO-side bug in this change.

The route passes the no-target `requestId` through to MCP, matching the intended browser's v4 UUID. Direct callers can supply other UUID forms accepted by FLUJO but rejected by MCP; those currently become `handoff_unverified` rather than route validation errors. This is contract polish for direct callers, not evidence of a false verified handoff.

Keep the action route draft/disabled until the pinned browser → running FLUJO worker → MCP run proves persisted case and handoff read-back, revocation and retry behavior, and ES/PT responses. The current focused tests use a mocked MCP and do not establish that joined acceptance. This comment is a self-authored review, not independent approval.

Exact-head follow-up at `5f2d65c1d229fef14ad98c67766357a4d9591873` (self-authored COMMENTED review). The narrow delta accepts an optional `requestId` on guarded `prepare` and passes it to `verifiedHandoff` when the policy immediately hands off. The new wiring assertion checks that MCP receives the same `request_id` together with the pending handle and `missing_evidence` reason. This matches banking PR #16's stable-request-ID handoff contract; I found no new FLUJO-side regression in the delta. Typecheck, lint, isolated tests, release-safety checks and both production builds are green on this head; the broad test job is still running. The prior head's three focused banking suites passed 95 tests locally, but they used mocked MCP.

The direct-caller UUID validation difference remains minor: FLUJO's `z.string().uuid()` permits forms that Banking MCP rejects, so such calls can become `handoff_unverified` instead of route-level 400. The intended Savia browser generates canonical v4 UUIDs and aligns.

A private browser-origin HTTP → running FLUJO worker → stdio MCP joined trace did persist and read back one case and one HOF, but it was pinned to the *previous* heads (`41ff3ca` here, banking `26cf2e3`). This commit and banking's new status/retry code were not exercised by that trace. Keep the route draft/flag-off and issue #15 open until the same current build passes the ES/PT failure/recovery matrix and operator pickup gate. This is not independent approval.

Exact-head follow-up at `3a2bcd8`: the delta from the failing `5f2d65c` head is focused. `/v1/banking/action` now calls `assertUnlocked({ openai: true })` inside the workspace-selected handler before dispatch, matching the neighboring revoke route. The new route-wiring regression exercises locked 423 with no MCP call, then unlocked success. This addresses the missing-gate finding from the [prior broad CI failure](https://github.com/mario-andreschak/FLUJO/actions/runs/36628294558/job/109611315354); I found no new issue in this two-file diff.

The fresh exact-head CI run is still in progress, including the broad suite. Keep this PR draft and the customer action flag off until terminal CI and the banking PR #16 recovery fixes are reviewed. The earlier synthetic joined worker traces were pinned to `5f2d65c` and do not test locked-workspace behavior on this new head.

Exact-head review of 5944464 (draft), compared with 3a2bcd8: the prepare route now requires a request UUID, forwards it through the exact host-only grant as request_id to Banking MCP, and reuses it for a policy handoff. The route regression checks missing ID as 400 before MCP, verifies forwarded arguments and foreign-owner 404. The model tool allowlist remains three read-only tools; no graph or model dispatch changed. I found no blocking issue in this delta.

The prior 3a lock-gate CI finished SUCCESS, and an independent archived-commit route wiring suite passed 28/28 with mocked lock/MCP. At this head, lint, typecheck, isolated tests, both production builds and release-safety are green; the broad test job is still running. Joined current-head browser→worker→MCP recovery and banking PR #16's frontend saved-ID retry remain release gates. Keep action disabled. This is a self-authored COMMENTED review, not independent approval.
